chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Sama'ah from Abi Basir from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the free man who marries the slave-girl, he said: 'There is no harm if he is compelled to do so.'

key_terms.الْحُرِّ: The free man (as opposed to a slave)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a free man to marry a slave girl in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In the context of classical Shia jurisprudence, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a free man's marriage to his own female slave (milk al-yamin) is permissible specifically under the condition of necessity (idtirar), distinguishing it from a permanent, unrestricted union. This ruling is foundational in the chapter on contracts within Tahdhib al-Ahkam, reflecting the practical legal needs of the early Muslim community regarding concubinage and marital status. The emphasis on 'necessity' ensures that the union is not merely for pleasure but serves to regulate sexual relations within the household structure.
